answer:
Start the container with the `--gpus=all` flag, as shown in the Nvidia GPU section of the Docker docs:

```shell
docker run -d --gpus=all -v ollama:/root/.ollama -p 11434:11434 --name ollama ollama/ollama
```

The docs say: "docker run -d --gpus=all -v ollama:/root/.ollama -p 11434:11434 --name ollama ollama/ollama" [ollama/docs/docker.md (lines 45-61) > Nvidia GPU > Configure Docker to use Nvidia driver]

Before running this, the docs say you need the NVIDIA Container Toolkit installed and Docker configured to use the Nvidia driver. The docs give these commands: "sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker" and "sudo systemctl restart docker" [ollama/docs/docker.md (lines 45-61) > Nvidia GPU > Configure Docker to use Nvidia driver]. The toolkit itself is linked from "Install the [NVIDIA Container Toolkit]" [ollama/docs/docker.md (lines 1-9) > Nvidia GPU].

To confirm the container can see your GPUs, the troubleshooting docs suggest: "docker run --gpus all ubuntu nvidia-smi" [ollama/docs/troubleshooting.md (lines 88-103) > NVIDIA GPU Discovery > Linux NVIDIA Troubleshooting].

The provided context doesn't say how to run this on Windows natively. It only mentions GPU acceleration in Docker on Windows with WSL2: "GPU acceleration is available in Docker on Linux or Windows (with WSL2)" is not quoted verbatim, but the FAQ says: "The Ollama Docker container can be configured with GPU acceleration in Linux or Windows (with WSL2)." [ollama/docs/faq.md (lines 253-257) > How do I use Ollama with GPU acceleration in Docker?]
